designSummary:
Phase 35 turns socket registration on by default, adds an honest history list, and makes liveness and status truthful on the wire. Eleven tasks in four waves.

THE SHAPE: the wire opens FIRST (one geist/0.4 bump, single owner, one conformance regeneration — every downstream consumer needs those fields and the bump is the one renderer cliff), the default-on FLIP lands in the middle (only after rewind scoping, ownership/hygiene/cap, and the soak writer exist), and RESUME lands LAST because it composes the history index, the delta stream and the hardened spawn primitive.

Wave 1 (5 parallel, zero file overlap): T1 session-scopes `activeRewinds`; T2 owns the entire geist/0.4 wire bump including Phase 34's `answered` debt (the repo's own rule at ROADMAP.md:430-432 assigns it to "whoever next opens the wire"); T3 owns same-owner enforcement, reap-on-start, the two immortal-debris classes and the socket cap across both mirrored readers; T4 builds the first-line history enumerator and GET /history; T5 builds the rotating soak writer.

Wave 2: T6 flips default-on with a split catch (explicit --attachable stays fatal, implicit degrades with exactly one notice); T7 replaces the fail-open boolean git probe with a deadline-bounded quad-state and emits origin/attachable/resumable/status on the projection.

Wave 3: T8 makes the daemon the single fleet scanner and adds fleet_delta + fleet_resync; T9 hooks the soak writer into the nine named seams so it records from the day the default flips.

Wave 4: T10 makes the shipped console refuse to present history as steerable and apply deltas without reconnecting; T11 adds session_resume behind one hardened spawn primitive that also replaces the existing unguarded ["draht","start"] PATH spawn.

THE THREE FACTS THAT DRIVE EVERYTHING. (1) Today a socket-registration failure KILLS the session — main.ts:919-926 does process.exit(1) on any bind failure — and the commonest failure is not environmental, it is the ordinary `draht --continue` twin, because `continueRecent` reopens the same session file and therefore reuses the socket name. (2) There is not one getuid() call in coding-agent/src, geist-core/src or gateway/src; the 0700 directory mode is the only thing between another uid and a full read-write attach. (3) The only status computation in the repo is fail-open AND deadline-unbounded, and it lives in a package the gateway does not even depend on — R35-ALWAYS.8 is greenfield on the wire that actually ships.

tasks.brief:
GOAL: `isRewindInProgress()` is currently process-global. Make it session-scoped.

WHAT IS THERE NOW (all line numbers read with sed; re-verify before editing):
- /Users/exe008/draht/draht-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/core/checkpoints/rewind.ts:83 — `let activeRewinds = 0;` This is the ONLY module-level mutable binding in core/checkpoints, core/socket-server and core/builtins.
- rewind.ts:94-96 — `export function isRewindInProgress(): boolean { return activeRewinds > 0; }`
- rewind.ts:224-231 — `performRewind` does `activeRewinds++` then `try { return await runRewind(options); } finally { activeRewinds--; }`
- THE ONLY PRODUCTION READER: /Users/exe008/draht/draht-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/core/builtins/checkpoints.ts:89 — `if (isRewindInProgress()) return undefined;` inside `confirmRestore(targetEntryId, ctx, flow)`. Returning `undefined` there is indistinguishable from "user declined", so a leak silently suppresses a second session's file-restore offer.
- THE ONLY PRODUCTION WRITER: /Users/exe008/draht/draht-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:5235 — the single `performRewind({...})` call.

THE CHANGE:
1. rewind.ts: replace `let activeRewinds = 0` with `const activeRewinds = new Map<string, number>()`. Add a REQUIRED `sessionId: string` to `PerformRewindOptions`. `performRewind` increments/decrements under that key in the existing try/finally and DELETES the key when it reaches zero, so a long-lived process cannot accumulate one entry per session replacement.
2. Change the signature to `isRewindInProgress(sessionId: string): boolean`. Make the parameter REQUIRED, not optional — an optional parameter silently preserves today's process-wide answer at every call site the migration misses, which is the exact defect you are removing.
3. checkpoints.ts:89 becomes `if (isRewindInProgress(ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId())) return undefined;`. `ctx` is already in scope; `getSessionId` is already in the `ReadonlySessionManager` pick list (packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts:~231-248, implementation at ~:1060-1062) and `ExtensionContext.sessionManager` is typed as `ReadonlySessionManager` (packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/types.ts:~428). No new context field, no new extension API. Read it AT CALL TIME — that is what makes it survive session replacement.
4. interactive-mode.ts:5235 passes `sessionId: this.sessionManager.getSessionId()`. Do NOT touch `this.isRewindRunning` (declared ~:406, set ~:5232/:5255, read ~:2922) — it is already correctly instance-scoped and is the precedent the gate should have followed.

The roadmap acceptance says "a regression proves isRewindInProgress() is session-scoped with two concurrent attachable sessions in one process", but NO emitted-binary construct produces that state: there is exactly one `new InteractiveMode(` in the tree (main.ts:958), `performRewind` is reachable only from InteractiveMode, rpc/print modes have no rewind entry point, and subagents/`/duet` are CHILD processes (packages/coding-agent/src/core/builtins/subagent.ts:82 `DRAHT_BIN = process.execPath`, :249 `["--mode","json","-p","--no-session"]`, :270 `spawn(...)`). YOU ARE THE SOLE OWNER OF THE WIRE THIS PHASE. Every field Phase 35 needs lands in ONE bump, ONE migration note and ONE corpus regeneration. Nobody else may edit packages/geist-protocol/src/wire.ts, conformance/, or the mirrored socket types.

WHY EVERYTHING AT ONCE: every 0.x member is mutually incompatible and a 0.4 daemon hard-refuses a cached 0.3 renderer at `hello` with `version_mismatch` + close 1008 (ProtocolVersionSchema is a `z.literal`, wire.ts:50; this was verified live against a running daemon). Batching minimises the number of cliffs.

=== 1. AttachableSessionSchema (wire.ts:223-229) ===
Add, and RELAX pid:
- `origin: z.enum(["socket", "history"])`
- `attachable: z.boolean()`
- `resumable: z.boolean()`
- `status: z.enum(["clean", "dirty", "no_repo", "unknown"])`
- `statusAt: z.string().min(1).max(64).nullable()`
- `pid` becomes `.optional()` — a history row has no pid. This is a BREAKING field change, not an addition.
VOCABULARY RULING (do not improvise): `origin` values are `"socket"` and `"history"`, matching the phase acceptance text at /Users/exe008/draht/draht-mono/.planning/ROADMAP.md:446 verbatim ("origin:socket, attachable:true" / "origin:history, attachable:false, resumable:true"). Do NOT use "live".
STATUS RULING: four values, not a boolean, and never coerced back to a boolean anywhere. `no_repo` is its own value because on Oskar's real machine 54 of the 55 non-zero `git status` exits across 107 live cwds are "not a git repository" — a stable fact, not a transient failure. `unknown` is reserved for "git refused or timed out on a repo that exists" and must never collapse to `clean`. `statusAt` exists because the probe is deadline-bounded and cached, so every value ages and honest liveness means saying when it was observed; it is also the debounce basis for status deltas.

=== 2. FleetFrameSchema (wire.ts:236-240) ===
Add `epoch: z.string().min(1)` and `seq: z.number().int().nonnegative()` so a snapshot and the deltas that follow it are orderable on one connection.

=== 3. NEW FleetDeltaFrameSchema (server → client) ===
`{ type: "fleet_delta", epoch: string, seq: number, changes: Array<{kind:"appeared", session: AttachableSession} | {kind:"disappeared", id: string} | {kind:"changed", session: AttachableSession}> }` with a sane `.max()` on the array.
CRITICAL: `appeared` and `changed` carry the FULL session body, never just an id. Resuming a session reuses the SAME session id with a NEW pid and startedAt (verified by running it), so the normal resume trace for one key is `disappeared(X)` then `appeared(X)`. A client that coalesces on id, or merges rather than replaces, renders the dead pid. Say that in the schema's doc comment.

=== 4. NEW FleetResyncFrameSchema (client → server) ===
`{ type: "fleet_resync" }` — a DISTINCT post-authentication verb. It cannot be spelled as a repeated `hello` (refused `invalid_frame` + close 1008) and it cannot be an unknown type (refused `unknown_type` + close 1008, which KILLS the connection). Both refusals were confirmed live.

=== 5. NEW session_resume pair ===
Client → server: `{ type: "session_resume", sessionId: z.string().min(1).max(128) }` — an ID ONLY. No path, no command, no argv. That is what makes it not an arbitrary-execution surface.
Server → client: `{ type: "session_resumed", sessionId, ok: z.boolean(), code: z.enum(["resumed","already_live","not_found","cwd_missing","refused","spawn_failed","timeout"]), message: <safeText helper already used in this file> }`.

=== 6. ServerHelloFrameSchema (wire.ts:184-191) ===
Add `capabilities: z.array(z.string().max(64)).max(32)`. Today `server_hello` carries only `{protocol, version, server, limits}` and there is no channel through which a daemon can say it accepts `fleet_resync`. `attach` already established this pattern in 0.3 (wire.ts:109-121). Later tasks gate `fleet_delta` emission on a capability the client declared, exactly as permission frames are gated.

The repo's own recorded rule at /Users/exe008/draht/draht-mono/.planning/ROADMAP.md:430-432 says "Owner: whoever next opens the wire". Phase 35 opens the wire. `answered` is a NEUTRAL member: it grants nothing and must read fail-closed at every consumer. VOCABULARY AND AUDIT-ROW CORRECTNESS ONLY — no behaviour change, no new code paths.

tasks.title: Same-owner attach, reap-on-start, immortal-debris closure and a live-socket cap
tasks.brief:
YOU OWN BOTH MIRRORED READERS. These two files implement the same scan twice on purpose and MUST change identically. `scripts/check-geist-protocol.mjs`'s mirror clause covers the 12 relayed FRAMES only (MIRRORED_FRAMES at :78-101) — it does NOT cover reaping rules, and the two readers have ALREADY DRIFTED (see (b3)). Do not assume that gate protects you.

=== A. SAME-OWNER (R35-ALWAYS.3) ===
BASELINE FACT: there is NOT ONE `getuid()` call in packages/coding-agent/src, packages/geist-core/src or packages/gateway/src. The 0700 mode on the sockets directory is the only same-owner protection that exists. It was demonstrated that a world-writable directory containing a 0666 socket and a lock naming root's pid 1 is listed as a live attachable session by BOTH readers and would be dialled by the bridge.

A1. `SocketServer.start()` — /Users/exe008/draht/draht-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/core/socket-server/socket-server.ts:166-174. Today it does `await mkdir(socketDir, {recursive:true, mode:0o700}); await chmod(socketDir, 0o700);` and then `await this.#claimLock()`. BEFORE `#claimLock()`, add an ownership assertion on the directory: `lstat` it, require a real directory (not a symlink), `uid === process.getuid()`, and `(mode & 0o077) === 0`. REFUSE with a typed error rather than silently chmod'ing a directory that is not ours. Keep the mkdir+chmod for the create path.
RULING on "0700 per-uid socket directory" — it is an ASSERTION, not a new `sockets/<uid>/` path segment. A uid segment costs sun_path budget (the default path `/Users/<user>/.draht/agent/sockets/<36-char uuid>.sock` is already 76 bytes of the ~104 limit) and would force the deliberately duplicated `SOCKETS_DIR_NAME` constant in geist-core (socket-sessions.ts:41) to move in lockstep. Assert ownership; do NOT move the path.

A2. Both scan loops — coding-agent discovery.ts:38-81 and geist-core socket-sessions.ts:135-169. `stat`/`statSync` the `.sock` AND the `.lock` and SKIP any entry whose `uid !== process.getuid()`. A foreign-uid entry is never listed, and (unlike today) a foreign-uid LOCK becomes reapable rather than permanently busy.

A3. The bridge — /Users/exe008/draht/draht-mono/packages/geist-core/src/attach/attach-bridge.ts:~676-688. Today the only gate between an AttachFrame and `connect()` is a path-separator test plus membership in `listAttachableSessions`. Between the liveness check and the `connect()`, re-`lstat` the `.sock` and the `.lock` and refuse unless BOTH are owned by `process.getuid()`. The comment at ~:673-677 already says the confinement is restated locally so a change to how liveness is decided cannot weaken it — the ownership check belongs in exactly that spot, not only inside `listAttachableSessions`.

A4. KEEP the EPERM-means-alive rule (socket-sessions.ts:63-71, discovery.ts:141-149 — `kill(pid,0)` returning EPERM is deliberately read as ALIVE). The uid check is what makes it safe: today a lock naming root's pid 1 refuses that session id FOREVER regardless of age (verified at 1 hour old); with A2 in place that lock is foreign-uid and reapable, which cures pid-recycling poisoning without giving `UNWRITTEN_LOCK_STALE_MS` a second meaning.

=== B. HYGIENE (R35-ALWAYS.4) ===
B1. REAP ON START. `start()` today touches ONLY this session's two paths. Add a full-directory sweep before the cap check. MEASURED: 25 emitted-binary start/SIGKILL cycles currently leave exactly 50 files (25 .sock + 25 .lock), strictly linear, zero reaped — reaping happens ONLY on discovery, so a machine where no phone or daemon ever calls GET /fleet grows without bound. The phase acceptance is "50 sequential start/kill cycles leave zero .sock/.lock files", which is unmeetable without this. Cost measured: a scan of 1000 live pairs is 12-32 ms; a sweep that reaps 1000 dead pairs is 106 ms. If you decide to bound or sample the sweep, write down the reasoning.

B2. CLOSE THE TWO IMMORTAL DEBRIS CLASSES, in BOTH readers:
  (i) a `.sock` with NO `.lock`. discovery.ts:56 does `if (!existsSync(lockPath)) continue;` and socket-sessions.ts:149-150 does `const lock = readLock(lockPath); if (!lock) continue;` — both `continue` WITHOUT reaping. Two such orphans have sat in Oskar's real ~/.draht/agent/sockets since 2026-08-21. Any test that counts leftover files must handle this or it passes on a machine that is already leaking.
  (ii) a REGULAR FILE named `<id>.sock`. Neither reader can remove it.
Define a grace window (recommend: older than `UNWRITTEN_LOCK_STALE_MS`) and reap. Write down the rule.

B3. FIX THE DRIFT that makes (ii) worse: discovery.ts:43 adds the id to `sessionIdsWithSocket` BEFORE the `isSocket()` test at :49-50, shielding the lock from `reapOrphanedLocks`; socket-sessions.ts:143-147 adds to `withSocket` only AFTER `isSocket()` passes. Make discovery.ts match socket-sessions.ts.

B4. BOUND READABLE-PID LOCKS. `UNWRITTEN_LOCK_STALE_MS = 10_000` (socket-server.ts:39) governs ONLY the no-readable-pid case, via `#lockIsAbandoned` (~:513-521) called from `#claimLock` (~:490-497). GOAL: `session_resume` over the public protocol turns a history session into a live one that joins the fleet with NO client reconnect.

=== THE REQUIREMENT NAMES THE WRONG MECHANISM — THIS IS THE CORRECTION ===
R35-ALWAYS.9 says "through the existing `--resume` path". `--resume` TAKES NO VALUE: packages/coding-agent/src/cli/args.ts:88-89 is `else if (arg === "--resume" || arg === "-r") { result.resume = true; }`, and main.ts:378-393 calls `selectSession(...)`, a full-screen TUI picker. Run headless it paints 2,742 bytes of ANSI and exits on stdin EOF. A daemon cannot use it.
NEITHER can a bare id. `resolveSessionPath` (main.ts:220-245) forks three ways on the argument SHAPE; a bare id found in ANOTHER project reaches the interactive fork prompt at main.ts:341-348 (`promptConfirm("Fork this session into current directory?")`, main.ts:249-259, which uses `createInterface({input: process.stdin})` with NO TTY check). PROVEN: spawned from a different cwd with stdin at /dev/null, the child prints the question, EOF answers "no", it prints "Aborted." and EXITS 0 having started nothing — indistinguishable from success to any caller. This is the single most likely way a naive implementation fails.
THE DAEMON-SAFE FORM, verified by running it: `--session <ABSOLUTE .jsonl path> --attachable --mode rpc`. The path branch skips the fork prompt entirely and runs in the SESSION's cwd regardless of the spawner's cwd. `--mode rpc` is REQUIRED: with no TTY, `resolveAppMode` (main.ts:118-129) falls through to print mode and the process answers once and exits, so the socket appears and vanishes.
THE KEYSTONE, verified: a resumed session KEEPS THE SAME session id, so it binds the SAME socket path and appends to the SAME .jsonl (id preservation at packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts:~1613-1632; socket named from `header.id` at session-integration.ts:112-119). `pid` and `startedAt` change. A history entry and its resumed live entry share ONE wire key — the client's card does not need re-keying, and the fleet trace is `disappeared(X)` then `appeared(X)`.

=== A. ONE HARDENED SPAWN PRIMITIVE — NEW packages/gateway/src/session/spawn-primitive.ts ===
Resume is process creation from a remote frame, so it inherits Phase 36's exec-surface requirements EARLY. Build it once, here, and reduce both callers to it.
WHAT IS FREE BY CONSTRUCTION (R36-SPAWN.1/.8): the client names ONLY a session id (the wire frame has no path and no command field); the daemon resolves it against its OWN history index; same id space by construction.
WHAT YOU MUST BUILD, not default into:
- R36-SPAWN.2: resolve the draht binary to a CANONICAL ABSOLUTE path, never PATH. Every spawn in the repo today is a bare PATH string.
